answer: Admission is a clearing market, not a toll booth. Each epoch the levy a seat pays equals the lowest winning bid, so every extra identity admitted raises the price all seats pay; a farm opening k seats lifts the clearing bid roughly k steps and then pays that inflated levy on every one, about k-squared in total. Nothing is stamped in a cheap pigment of novelty here, since a per-key opal bond must be posted and revalued each round, and the public onyx ledger makes each new clone raise the cost of the clones beside it.
